function.name: execute
function.description: Execute a shell command inside the Kali Linux sandbox. Common recon tools are pre-installed (nmap, sqlmap, nuclei, ffuf, subfinder, httpx, etc.). Use this for any external binary. Examples: {"command": "subfinder -d example.com -o output/subdomains.txt"} or {"command": "nmap -sV -p 1-1000 target"}. Avoid interactive tools; prefer one-shot commands. Long-running tools may be terminated if they exceed per_tool_timeout_seconds.

command.description: Shell command to run inside sandbox (executed via bash -c). Pipes are allowed; avoid interactive prompts.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (default 600). Maximum allowed is 3600.

function.name: advanced_fuzz
function.description: Parameter fuzzing for web vulnerabilities. Tests for SQL injection, XSS, SSRF, IDOR, SSTI, mass assignment, and more. Can run Phase 2 advanced tests (cloud SSRF probes, GraphQL introspection, race conditions) when enabled. Target URL and parameters should be provided for meaningful results. Example: target="https://api.example.com/v1/users", parameters=["id","user_id"], vuln_types=["sql_injection","xss"], method="GET". Returns findings with severity, confidence, and evidence.

phase2.description: Enable Phase 2 advanced tests (default true). Includes SSRF to 169.254.169.254, GraphQL introspection, race condition probing.

ssrf_params.description: List of parameters to test for SSRF with cloud metadata probes.

race_params.description: Parameters to test for race conditions.

function.name: run_parallel_agents
function.description: Launch multiple parallel AIRecon scout agents on multiple targets simultaneously, bounded by a concurrency semaphore.

targets.description: List of targets/domains to scan in parallel.

prompt.description: The exact prompt/directive for the parallel agents to execute on each target.

function.name: browser_action
function.description: Control a Playwright-powered headless Chromium browser for navigation, DOM interaction, auth flows, logs, and evidence capture. Actions: launch, goto, click, type, scroll_down/up, back/forward, new_tab/switch_tab/close_tab/list_tabs, wait, execute_js (optional parallel across open tabs), double_click, hover, press_key, save_pdf, screenshot, view_source, get_console_logs, get_network_logs, login_form, handle_totp, save_auth_state, inject_cookies, oauth_authorize, check_auth_status, wait_for_element, solve_captcha. Notes: screenshot saves a PNG under workspace_root/screenshots and returns screenshot_path; save_pdf returns pdf_saved; execute_js returns js_result (truncated to ~5000 chars) with page state.

action.description: The action to perform. Key actions: execute_js — run JS in page; use js_code; returns js_result + state; parallel=true runs across open tabs. save_pdf — export page as PDF to file_path (workspace-relative). screenshot — capture PNG to workspace_root/screenshots; returns screenshot_path. login_form — authenticate; handle_totp — TOTP; solve_captcha — auto-solve (captcha_type + sitekey). wait_for_element — dynamic wait. get_console_logs / get_network_logs — fetch logs. Full list: launch, goto, click, type, scroll_*, navigation, tab management (new_tab/switch_tab/close_tab/list_tabs), execute_js, save_pdf, screenshot, view_source, console/network logs, auth actions, wait_for_element, solve_captcha.

js_code.description: JavaScript code to execute (REQUIRED for execute_js action). Result is truncated to ~5000 chars. Examples: 'document.querySelectorAll("a").length', 'localStorage.getItem("token")', 'JSON.stringify(performance.getEntries())'. Result includes page state (url, title) and js_result field.

parallel.description: For execute_js only: when true, run the same JS code concurrently across ALL open tabs. Useful for gathering comparative data or extracting same info from multiple pages. Do not set tab_id when using parallel=true. Returns parallel_results dict mapping tab_id to individual results.

file_path.description: Path to save PDF (REQUIRED for save_pdf action, should end with .pdf). Path is relative to workspace root. Saves rendered page to PDF. Returns pdf_saved path in response state.

username.description: Username or email for login_form action.

username_selector.description: CSS selector for username/email field in login_form (comma-separated fallbacks). Default covers: input[type=email], input[name=username/user/email/login/mail], input[autocomplete=username/email], #username/#email/#user/#login. Override when default fails — first call view_source to find the correct selector.

password_selector.description: CSS selector for password field in login_form. Default: input[type='password']. Override for non-standard forms.

submit_selector.description: CSS selector for submit button in login_form (comma-separated fallbacks). Default tries: button[type=submit], input[type=submit], button:has-text('Log in/Login/Sign in/Continue/Next/Submit'). Override when default fails.

totp_secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret for handle_totp action. Generates a fresh RFC 6238 code automatically. Example: 'JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'. If rejected, call handle_totp again immediately (new 30s window). For 8-digit codes use totp_digits=8. For 60s period use totp_period=60.

multi_step.description: For login_form: set true for username-first flows (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, enterprise SSO) where password field only appears AFTER submitting the username. Workflow: fill username → click Next → wait for password field → fill password → submit.

totp_digits.description: For handle_totp: number of digits in the TOTP code. Default: 6 (standard RFC 6238). Use 8 for enterprise apps that require 8-digit codes.

totp_period.description: For handle_totp: TOTP time step in seconds. Default: 30 (standard). Use 60 for older/non-standard apps with 60-second windows.

wait_selector.description: For wait_for_element: CSS selector to wait for. Example: 'div.dashboard', '#logout-button', '.error-message'.

wait_timeout.description: For wait_for_element: timeout in seconds. Default: 10.

wait_state.description: For wait_for_element: element state to wait for. Default: 'visible'.

captcha_type.description: For solve_captcha: type of CAPTCHA. Choose 'recaptcha' for Google reCAPTCHA, 'hcaptcha' for hCaptcha, 'cloudflare_turnstile' for Cloudflare Turnstile, or 'unknown' if undetermined.

sitekey.description: For solve_captcha: the sitekey (public key) identifier for the CAPTCHA challenge. Usually found in data-sitekey attribute or challenge parameters.

cookies.description: Array of cookie objects [{name, value, domain, path}] for inject_cookies action.

oauth_url.description: Alias for url (legacy). If provided, treated as url for oauth_authorize.

callback_prefix.description: Expected callback URL prefix for oauth_authorize to detect redirect completion.

function.name: request_user_input
function.description: Pause the agent and request user-provided input (e.g., CAPTCHA, TOTP/OTP, password, or manual confirmation) before continuing.

prompt.description: Clear instruction to the user explaining exactly what to enter. Example: 'Please enter the 6-digit TOTP code from your authenticator app for target.com' or 'Solve the CAPTCHA shown in screenshot_20240101_120000.png and enter the text here'.

input_type.description: Type of expected input. 'totp' = 6-digit time-based code, 'captcha' = CAPTCHA solution text, 'otp' = one-time password (SMS/email), 'password' = sensitive credential, 'text' = anything else.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for user input in seconds. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Use shorter timeout for time-sensitive inputs like TOTP.

function.name: create_file
function.description: Create a new file in the workspace. Overwrites if exists.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root (e.g. 'output/results.txt'). Do NOT include a leading 'workspace/' prefix — it is stripped automatically.

content.description: Content to write to the file.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a file from the workspace with optional offset/limit pagination for large outputs.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root (e.g. 'output/nmap.txt'). Do NOT include a leading 'workspace/' prefix — it is stripped automatically.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed). Default: 0 (start of file).

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Default: 500. Use smaller values for very large files.

function.name: list_files
function.description: List files and directories in the workspace with metadata; prefer this over execute ls.

path.description: Directory path to list (relative to workspace, e.g. 'output/', 'tools/', or leave empty for the target root). Default: target root.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web via SearXNG (DuckDuckGo fallback). Supports full Google dork operators when SearXNG is configured: site:, filetype:, inurl:, intitle:, ext:, -inurl:, cache:. Use for: (1) CVE/PoC research — 'CVE-2024-1234 exploit PoC github'; (2) Google dorking for sensitive exposure — 'site:target.com filetype:env', 'site:target.com inurl:admin', 'site:target.com ext:sql', 'intitle:index.of target.com backup'; (3) technology fingerprinting — 'site:target.com powered by X'; (4) credential/config leaks — 'site:target.com ext:yaml password', 'site:target.com filetype:log'. Combine operators for precision: 'site:target.com (filetype:pdf OR filetype:xls) confidential'. DuckDuckGo fallback supports basic operators but not wildcard site:*.

query.description: Search query. Supports dork operators: site:, filetype:, inurl:, intitle:, ext:, -inurl:. Examples: 'site:target.com filetype:env', 'inurl:admin site:target.com', 'CVE-2024-1234 PoC exploit'.

max_results.description: Maximum results to return (default: 10, max: 50). Use 20-30 for thorough dorking campaigns.

function.name: create_vulnerability_report
function.description: Create a FINAL confirmed vulnerability report under the active target's vulnerabilities/ directory. Call this only after you have reproducible PoC evidence and concrete impact. Never use it for hypotheses, raw observations, methodology, or todo items; use create_note for those. Required fields are: title, description, target, poc_description, and poc_script_code. The target can be a URL/host or a local file/folder reference tied to the active workspace target. Optional fields include impact, technical_analysis, remediation_steps, endpoint, method, flag, cve, suggested_fix, and the 8 CVSS base metrics.

title.description: Concise finding title, e.g. 'SQL Injection in /login' or 'Path Traversal in archive extractor'.

target.description: Affected target. Use URL/host for remote findings, or a local file/folder/workspace path when analyzing code or uploaded artifacts.

description.description: Clear vulnerability summary tied to observed behavior and evidence.

poc_description.description: How the proof of concept works and what behavior confirmed the issue.

poc_script_code.description: Actual exploit, payload, code snippet, or reproduction command. This is mandatory.

impact.description: Concrete attacker outcome: unauthorized data access, privilege change, code execution, service impact, etc.

attack_vector.description: Optional CVSS AV metric: N, A, L, or P.

attack_complexity.description: Optional CVSS AC metric: L or H.

privileges_required.description: Optional CVSS PR metric: N, L, or H.

user_interaction.description: Optional CVSS UI metric: N or R.

scope.description: Optional CVSS S metric: U or C.

confidentiality.description: Optional CVSS C metric: N, L, or H.

integrity.description: Optional CVSS I metric: N, L, or H.

availability.description: Optional CVSS A metric: N, L, or H.

endpoint.description: Optional affected endpoint, route, or file path.

method.description: Optional HTTP method or protocol used in the PoC.

cve.description: Optional CVE ID if directly applicable.

suggested_fix.description: Optional code/config patch or exact fix snippet.

flag.description: Optional flag value if captured during CTF/exercise.

cwe.description: Optional CWE identifier(s) for the weakness class, e.g. 'CWE-79' or 'CWE-89'.

owasp.description: Optional OWASP category, e.g. 'A03:2021-Injection' or 'API1:2023 - BOLA'.

function.name: quick_fuzz
function.description: Run a fast fuzz scan on a URL using common payloads (SQLi, XSS, traversal, SSTI). If params are omitted, it uses a small default list (q, search, id, page).

params.description: Optional list of parameters to fuzz. If omitted, defaults to common params: q, search, id, page.

function.name: deep_fuzz
function.description: Run thorough interactive fuzzing with chain discovery after initial hints from quick_fuzz or advanced_fuzz.

params.description: Optional list of parameters to fuzz. If omitted, auto-discovers high-priority targets.

vuln_types.description: Optional vulnerability types to test. If omitted, tests all available types.

function.name: generate_wordlist
function.description: Generate a targeted payload/parameter wordlist from internal data and save it to the workspace for ffuf/feroxbuster.

output_file.description: Filename to save the wordlist (e.g. 'sqli_payloads.txt'). Saved inside output/ folder.

vuln_types.description: Filter payload categories to include. Available: sql_injection, xss, command_injection, path_traversal, ssti, xxe, ssrf, idor, mass_assignment, parameter_pollution, jwt, graphql, race_condition. Omit to include ALL categories.

max_combinations.description: Cap on parameter name mutation variants appended after payloads (default: 300, max: 1000).

function.name: caido_list_requests
function.description: Query Caido history with HTTPQL filters and return request IDs, methods, paths, and statuses.

function.name: caido_send_request
function.description: Replay or modify HTTP requests through Caido using a request_id or raw HTTP payload.

request_id.description: Caido request ID to replay (from caido_list_requests). Optional if raw_http provided.

raw_http.description:
Full plain-text raw HTTP request to send (e.g. 'GET /api/user?id=2 HTTP/1.1
Host: target.com

'). Do NOT base64-encode — executor handles encoding.

port.description: Target port (default: 443 for TLS, 80 for plain)

function.name: caido_automate
function.description: Start a Caido Automate fuzzing session using §FUZZ§ markers to define injection points.

raw_http.description:
Full raw HTTP request with §FUZZ§ markers at injection points (e.g. 'POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: target.com

{"user":"admin","pass":"§FUZZ§"}')

payloads.description: List of payloads to inject at §FUZZ§ positions (e.g. ["' OR 1=1--", "admin", "<script>alert(1)</script>"])

function.name: caido_get_findings
function.description: Fetch findings/annotations stored in Caido, including title, description, reporter, and related request data.

function.name: caido_intercept
function.description: Control Caido intercept: check status, pause/resume capture, list queued messages, forward (optionally modified), or drop.

action.description: Action to perform: status (get intercept state: RUNNING/PAUSED), pause (stop capturing), resume (start capturing), list (show queued messages), forward (forward a queued message), drop (discard a queued message)

message_id.description: ID of the intercept message to forward or drop (from list action)

raw_http.description: Modified raw HTTP request to send when forwarding (optional — omit to forward unchanged)

function.name: caido_sitemap
function.description: Browse Caido sitemap nodes (hosts/directories/endpoints); pass parent_id to drill into child nodes.

parent_id.description: Node ID to list children for (from a previous caido_sitemap call). Omit to list root hosts.

function.name: caido_set_scope
function.description: Set Caido proxy scope to focus capture and testing on specific hosts. Allowlisted hosts are captured; denylisted hosts are excluded.

function.name: spawn_agent
function.description: Spawn a specialist subagent for deep investigation of a specific finding/endpoint and merge results back to the session.

task.description: Specific investigation task for the subagent (e.g. 'Test /api/login for SQL injection, parameter: username')

target.description: Target URL or domain for the subagent (e.g. 'https://target.com/api/login')

specialist.description: Type of specialist: sqli (SQL injection), xss (Cross-site scripting), ssrf (Server-side request forgery), lfi (Local file inclusion/path traversal), recon (Reconnaissance only), exploit (General exploitation), analyzer (Code/config analysis), reporter (Report generation)

function.name: schemathesis_fuzz
function.description: Run schema-aware API fuzzing with Schemathesis against OpenAPI/Swagger specs to detect crashes, auth bypasses, and injections.

schema_url.description: URL or file path to the OpenAPI/Swagger spec (e.g. 'https://target.com/openapi.json', 'https://target.com/swagger.yaml', '/workspace/target/output/api-spec.json'). Common paths to try: /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api/docs, /api-docs, /v1/openapi.json.

base_url.description: Base URL of the API to test against (e.g. 'https://target.com/api/v1'). If omitted, uses the server URL from the schema.

auth_header.description: Authorization header value to include in every request (e.g. 'Bearer eyJhbGc...' or 'Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz'). Use session auth_tokens if available.

checks.description: Schemathesis checks to run. Available: not_a_server_error, status_code_conformance, content_type_conformance, response_schema_conformance, negative_data_rejection. Omit for all checks.

max_examples.description: Max test cases per endpoint (default: 30). Increase for deeper coverage, decrease for speed.

function.name: code_analysis
function.description: Run Semgrep static analysis on source code in the sandbox to detect security issues (OWASP/CWE patterns).

target_path.description: Path to scan inside the workspace (e.g. 'output/repo-clone', '.' for current target root). Relative to the target workspace directory.

rules.description: Semgrep rule sets to use (e.g. ['p/security-audit', 'p/owasp-top-ten']). If omitted, uses all default security rules.

languages.description: Filter to specific languages (e.g. ['python', 'javascript', 'java']). If omitted, scans all detected languages.

function.name: http_observe
function.description: Send raw HTTP requests from the sandbox and return full response details; supports baseline save and response diffing.

method.description: HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS. Default: GET

headers.description: Additional request headers as key-value pairs (e.g. {"Authorization": "Bearer token", "Content-Type": "application/json"})

save_as.description: Name to store this response as a baseline (e.g. 'baseline_normal', 'baseline_auth'). Stored in session for later diffing.

compare_to.description: Name of a previously saved baseline to diff against. Shows what changed between the baseline and this response.

follow_redirects.description: Whether to follow redirects. Default: false — keep false to observe Location header for redirect-based vulnerabilities (open redirect, SSRF via redirect).

function.name: record_hypothesis
function.description: Create or update a security hypothesis with status (pending/testing/confirmed/refuted) and optional evidence.

claim.description: The security hypothesis claim. E.g. 'The /api/user endpoint is vulnerable to IDOR via user_id parameter' or 'Login form is vulnerable to SQLi in username field'.

test_plan.description: What specific test/payload to run to verify or refute this hypothesis. E.g. 'Send GET /api/user?user_id=2 while authenticated as user 1. If response returns user 2 data, IDOR is confirmed.'

status.description: Current status: 'pending'=not yet tested, 'testing'=currently verifying, 'confirmed'=vulnerability proven, 'refuted'=tested and not vulnerable.

hypothesis_id.description: ID of an existing hypothesis to update (e.g. 'h_5_2'). If omitted, a new hypothesis is created.

evidence.description: Evidence supporting or refuting the hypothesis. Include HTTP response snippets, diff results, or tool output that proves/disproves the claim.

phase.description: Pipeline phase where this hypothesis was formed (RECON/ANALYSIS/EXPLOIT). Default: current phase.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Dynamically load a skill file (vulnerability methodology, technology guide, or protocol deep-dive) into the current session. Skills enhance analysis capabilities for specific contexts. Use when you discover a new technology or vulnerability type that requires specialized knowledge.

skills.description: Comma-separated list of skill file paths relative to the skills/ directory. Examples: 'vulnerabilities/sql_injection.md', 'technologies/react.md', 'vulnerabilities/xss.md'. Use read_file to explore available skills if uncertain. Paths are case-sensitive.

replace_skills.description: If true, replace currently loaded skills with these ones. If false (default), add to existing skills. Use replace=true when switching to a completely different assessment type.

function.name: python_session
function.description: Start or continue a lightweight Python exec/eval session with state persistence. Variables, functions, and imports persist across calls. Pre-imports: os, sys, json, re, base64, hashlib, random, datetime, pathlib.Path, urllib.parse helpers; requests is available only if installed. Session auto-terminates after 300s of inactivity. Parameters: session_id (optional, defaults to 'default'), code (required). Returns: output (stdout/stderr), result (last expression if any), session_state (variables dict), error (if any).

session_id.description: Optional session identifier. Use named sessions to maintain separate contexts. Default: 'default'.

code.description: Python code to execute. Can be multiple lines. Use print() for output. Last expression's value is returned in 'result'. Example: "import requests; resp = requests.get('https://example.com'); print(resp.status_code); resp.text[:200]"

function.name: edit_file

path.description: Path to file (workspace-relative, e.g., "output/script.py"). Must exist.

old_str.description: Exact text to find and replace. Must match exactly including newlines and indentation. Get the exact string by reading the file first.

new_str.description: Replacement text. Should maintain consistent formatting.

function.name: think
function.description: Explicitly record a reasoning step, hypothesis, or analytical thought. This captures your thinking process for later review, debugging, and transparency. Thoughts are saved to the session and written to output/thoughts_<phase>.log. Use this before critical decisions, when forming hypotheses, or when analyzing complex evidence. Parameters: thought (required) - your reasoning, hypothesis, or analysis. Optional: category ("hypothesis", "analysis", "decision", "question", "insight"), confidence (0.0-1.0 if supported). Example: {"thought": "The SQL error suggests a MySQL backend. Union-based injection likely works. Testing with '1' UNION SELECT NULL--"}

thought.description: Your reasoning, hypothesis, or analytical observation. Be specific and actionable.

category.description: Type of thought. Helps organize thinking trace.

confidence.description: Confidence level 0.0-1.0 if your thought is a hypothesis or analysis. Optional.

function.name: create_note
function.description: Create a structured WORKING note with category, tags, and optional metadata. Notes persist across the session and can be searched later. Categories: vulnerability, methodology, finding, question, plan, observation, todo. Use notes for hypotheses, raw observations, task tracking, methodology, and draft evidence. Notes are NOT final vulnerability reports and do NOT write to vulnerabilities/; use create_vulnerability_report for confirmed findings. Parameters: category (required), title (required), content (required), tags (optional array). Returns note_id and status. Example: {"category": "vulnerability", "title": "SQL Injection in login", "content": "Union-based SQLi on username field...", "tags": ["sqli", "critical", "auth"]}

content.description: Full note content. Supports markdown formatting.

function.name: list_notes
function.description: List all notes with optional filtering by category or tag. Returns note metadata (id, title, category, tags, created_at) without full content. Use to browse or find notes. Parameters: category (optional filter), tag (optional filter), limit (default 50). Example: {"category": "vulnerability"} or {"tag": "critical"}

limit.description: Maximum number of notes to return (default 50).

function.name: export_notes_wiki
function.description: Export all notes to a single wiki markdown file for documentation. Useful at the end of engagement to generate organized report appendix. Parameters: output_path (optional, default: current target's "notes/wiki.md"). Returns export status and path. Example: {"output_path": "output/wiki_notes.md"}

output_path.description: Output file path (workspace-relative). Default: current target's notes/wiki.md

function.name: search_notes
function.description: Full-text search across all notes. Returns matching notes with snippets showing context. Parameters: query (required string), category (optional filter), limit (default 20). Use to find specific information previously documented. Example: {"query": "SQL injection", "category": "vulnerability"}

function.name: dataset_search
function.description: Search the local security knowledge base (installed via airecon-dataset). Retrieves relevant Q&A pairs, techniques, payloads, and CVE knowledge from locally indexed HuggingFace datasets. Use when you need reference knowledge about: specific vulnerability classes, exploit techniques, CVE details, CTF techniques, bug bounty methodology, or payload examples. Example: {"query": "SQL injection bypass WAF", "limit": 3} or {"query": "SSRF cloud metadata", "category": "vulnerability"}. Returns matching knowledge entries from the local dataset index.

query.description: Search query — use specific technical terms for best results (e.g. 'XSS filter bypass', 'IDOR privilege escalation', 'CVE-2021-44228 log4j').

function.name: read_note
function.description: Retrieve the full content of a specific note by ID. Use after listing or searching notes to view complete details. Parameters: note_id (required). Returns the full note object with title, category, content, tags, timestamps. Example: {"note_id": "note_20260406_143022_a1b2c3d4"}

note_id.description: Unique note identifier (from create_note, list_notes, or search_notes results).
